maps.title: After Krishna Left · Day 01 · Aftermath of Krishna's Departure

nodeData.note: SB 1.14.1–15.13 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Arjuna has been gone to Dvaraka for seven months, and Yudhisthira reads in the omens around him that Krishna has left the world. Maharaj uses each sign of Kali to hold up a mirror to devotees: greed, pride, cheating and fear show that Krishna is not yet our real goal. As Arjuna returns in grief, Yudhisthira asks after everyone in Dvaraka and every lapse of duty, until only one reason is left: Krishna is gone. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 02 · Arjuna's Grief After Krishna Departs
nodeData.note: SB 1.15.1–12 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Arjuna can barely speak for grief, and Maharaj explains that this pain of separation is really the bliss of pure love. maps.title: After Krishna Left · Day 03 · Arjuna Recollects Krishna's Mercy

nodeData.note: SB 1.15.13–27 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Arjuna tells Yudhisthira how every victory of his life, from fighting for the demigods to crossing the Kaurava army, came only from Krishna's friendship, and how without Krishna his Gandiva failed against mere cowherds. Maharaj draws lessons on gratitude, full surrender and a living connection with the spiritual master, and asks that every act be measured by whether it pleases Krishna, ending with instructions that relieve the burning heart. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Arjuna, meditating on what Krishna did for him, recalls that even Indra and the demigods depended on his Gandiva bow, and that only Krishna's friendship carried him across the vast Kaurava army. Maharaj sums it up: by Krishna's mercy the impossible becomes possible.

nodeData.topic: Day 04 · Arjuna Focuses on Krishna's Words
nodeData.note: SB 1.15.28–35 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj shows how Arjuna, grieving for Krishna, is healed simply by remembering the instructions of the Gita, and draws the lesson that the guru's words carry their own potency when accepted fully and heard attentively. Yudhisthira and Kunti then turn towards going back to Godhead, and Maharaj explains why the Pandavas, for all their hardships, were never truly distressed. The class closes with the Yadus' departure as a thorn removing a thorn, the Lord's forms as eternal, and a few questions. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 05 · The Pandavas Retire and Depart
nodeData.note: SB 1.15.36–48 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. As Kali becomes fully manifest after Krishna's departure, Maharaja Yudhisthira enthrones the trained Pariksit, gives up every royal sign and walks north absorbed only in remembrance of Krishna, and his brothers, wife and mother follow him back to Godhead. Maharaj draws from this a practical message: train successors, leave the body smiling rather than lamenting, define the goal clearly and plan our Krishna consciousness, or maya will plan it for us. In the questions he explains why devotees sometimes become entangled after joining, and how to practise detachment at our own level. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 06 · Pandavas Leave Pariksit In Charge
nodeData.note: SB 1.15.49–16.15 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Chapter 15 closes with Vidura returning to his post as Yamaraja, Draupadi and Subhadra following their husbands, and the promise that hearing of the Pandavas' departure gives devotion. Chapter 16 opens with Pariksit ruling as an ideal devotee king: guided by brahmanas, performing sacrifices where even demigods appear, touring his kingdom and conquering the world while hearing everywhere the glories of Krishna. Many questions run through the class, on Vrindavan, chastity and a wife's own spiritual path, accepting difficulties, and how to answer people who doubt the scriptures. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 07 · How Was Earth After Krishna Left?
nodeData.note: SB 1.16.16–36 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Pariksit melts on hearing how Krishna served the Pandavas, and Maharaj asks how Krishna repays devotees who want nothing. Then Dharma as a bull, standing on one leg, questions the grieving Earth as a cow, and Maharaj walks through the symptoms of Kali: divided families, neglect of cows, women and children, lack of samskaras, and leaders who fear one another. Earth answers by remembering Krishna's qualities, and in the questions Maharaj advises temples to hire security so devotees can do their own duty. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Day 08 · Pariksit Sees a Special Cow and Bull
nodeData.note: SB 1.17.1–18 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Pariksit comes upon Kali, dressed as a king, beating a one-legged bull and a weeping cow, and confronts him with a ruler's force while assuring the victims of protection. Maharaj draws out a leader's duty to correct wrongdoing and why punishment helps the one punished. When Dharma will not blame anyone, Maharaj teaches that we ourselves are the cause of our suffering and should never react negatively. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The recording joins in the middle of the reading: Pariksit comes upon a sudra dressed as a king striking a bull and a cow, and the terrified bull stands trembling on one leg. The purports read these as signs of the age of Kali.

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · Why Did Pariksit Not Kill Kali?
nodeData.note: SB 1.17.19–45 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Pariksit sees that the bull is Dharma himself and that no one but our own karma, under Krishna's sanction, is to blame for suffering. Maharaj stresses that only a person of character has the right to correct others, and that sincerity in following the guru, not learning, is a speaker's potency. Kali surrenders and so cannot be killed, but he is banished to five places, and Pariksit restores the bull's legs by putting everything, even gold, in Krishna's service. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Maharaj recalls the previous class: material nature, the Supersoul and we ourselves each play a part in our happiness and distress, and Krishna gives the final sanction.

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · Maharaja Pariksit Cursed by a Boy
nodeData.note: SB 1.18.1–50 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Krishna protects Pariksit from his birth to his death, and while he rules, Kali cannot flourish, because constant chanting and hearing keep Kali away. Maharaj dwells on the science of hearing, the power of association and what makes Krishna supreme, then shows that the king's fatigue and anger at Samika Rishi were Krishna's arrangement to call his devotee home. The boy Sringi curses the king, and his father repents, showing a devotee's forbearance. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.
